card: Adds an optional `--mode` flag (`both`, `single`, or `combined`) to the `deterministic-fuzz-coverage` developer tool. Previously, the tool always executed both individual per-input checks and the combined multi-input run, making it slower and harder to isolate whether coverage non-determinism stemmed from per-input variance or cross-input state leakage. This allows developers debugging fuzz targets to run either check independently without altering default behavior.
changed_since_previous: The CLI argument changed from a positional argument to a named `--mode=<both|single|combined>` option.
evidence: Commit message: 'This makes it easier to distinguish per-input nondeterminism from cross-input state leakage. Good for debugging.'
problem: The tool previously ran both per-input checks and the combined single-process corpus check on every invocation. Developers troubleshooting fuzz non-determinism could not easily isolate per-input variance from cross-input global state leakage without running both stages.

risk.why: A mistake would only affect local coverage debugging when running the standalone Rust devtool.

summary: Adds an optional `--mode` flag (`both`, `single`, or `combined`) to the `deterministic-fuzz-coverage` developer tool. This lets developers execute either individual input determinism checks or the combined corpus run in isolation, while defaulting to running both.
